Its not meant to be easy and its not meant to be kind. Life is hard and people are put in our lives to assist us through our journey. When my father died, It fucked me up. It fucked me up for YEARS. Torturing myself about what I should've done different or could've done different. Since I am a father myself, I couldn't let myself slip into addiction or do something else equally cathartic and stupid. With no way to get it out, I just bottled it up and saved it for another day. I crammed myself into my work, taking on jobs that I really didn't have the time or resources for. I pushed everyone away, yet felt like I had to prove to them that I wasn't going to fall apart. While it may sound cliche, I wore a mask and lied and deluded myself until I finally believed it. There is a healthy and an unhealthy way to grieve. Grieving is necessary but if we don't do it right, we will only hurt ourselves and that IS NOT what our loved ones would want for us. I believe that every person who comes into our lives has a purpose. Something to teach us or guide us through while we do the same. I finally realized that my father played his role until the very end and that I was not doing my kids any favors being selfish. I got caught up in my feelings. I put my sadness above their happiness and that is not what my father would have wanted to see. You'll never get over the loss of loved ones. You're not supposed to, but rather drive on with the fond memories, that will help you to live a better life and perhaps make someone else's life better as a result. We owe it to ourselves and the memories of the fallen to use circumstances to our advantage. Make us stronger, make us braver, help us adapt quicker and love ourselves stronger.
